question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
question.explanation: ④번 위치의 had some church endured는 가정법 과거완료 구문에서 접속사 if가 생략되어 주어와 조동사가 도치되는 구조를 의도한 것처럼 보이지만, 본래 문장은 Unless 접속사 절로 주어인 the church와 완료형 동사 has endured가 결합한 일반 조건절 구조입니다. 만약 가정법 도치나 도치 구문을 적용하려면 context에 맞는 통사 구조가 성립해야 하나, 문맥상 '교회가 400도 이상의 온도를 견디지 못했다면'이라는 실제 사실에 기반한 조건부 부정(Unless)을 나타내므로, 명시적인 주어와 정동사의 일반적인 어순인 'Unless the church has endured'가 문법적이고 자연스럽습니다. had some church endured는 주어 자리에 생뚱맞은 some이 들어가고 시제 및 가정 도치 구조가 깨어진 비문이 되므로, 원래의 주어-동사 구조를 살린 has endured가 올바른 표현입니다.
keyPoints: 분사구문의 부사적 양보 표현(양보의 as 구문)에서 형용사/명사가 도치되어 문두에 위치하는 구문 구조 이해
명사를 후치 수식하는 관계사절 내의 동사 목적어 및 수식어 관계 파악
부사절 접속사 unless 뒤의 주어와 정동사(현재완료)의 올바른 어순과 수일치 파악

question.passageWithMarkers: The structure of glass is, frankly, a bit of a mess. Clear and perfect __(A) as__ it might appear to our eyes, down at the molecular level, glass looks more like a random ball-pit of atoms. The technical term for this mess depends on who you're asking: for some scientists it is an "amorphous solid," for others a "supercooled liquid." In theory it's both liquid and solid, though, given the way it behaves, in practice it's really the latter. In fact, at room temperature glass never behaves as a liquid, even an imperceptibly viscous __(B) one__, even over long periods of time (though it can "sweat" if you don't add enough lime to the mix). Those misshapen sheets of glass you sometimes __(C) see__ in old stained-glass windows, thicker at the bottom than the top, are generally not that way because the glass is slowly sinking over time. Unless the church __(D) had some church endured__ temperatures of more than 400˚C, the chances are they are uneven because that's the way they were blown and solidified in the first place. Flat glass was only developed in the nineteenth century and we had to wait until the middle of the twentieth century for truly flat, thin sheets of glass. The paradox is that, despite it being one of the very oldest human-made substances, scientists still struggle to comprehend why glass behaves the way it does. Glass seems __(E) to obey__ most molecular laws. As one glassmaker put it, glass is not a material; it's a state.
